grandcanyon.overview: The Grand Canyon offers some of the most dramatic hiking on Earth, dropping walkers below the rim into a vast, layered landscape of ancient rock. The famous corridor trails—Bright Angel and South Kaibab—descend steeply into the inner canyon, with unfolding views of the gorge and the Colorado River far below. These trails are strenuous, with every foot of descent requiring a steep climb back out. The mostly paved Rim Trail offers an easy alternative with continuous views along the edge.

great-smoky-mountains.overview: The Great Smoky Mountains offer hundreds of miles of trails through dense Appalachian forest to waterfalls and panoramic ridges. Hikers can climb Alum Cave Trail to Mount LeConte or walk sections of the Appalachian Trail out to Charlie's Bunion, with easy riverside paths, steep rocky ascents and multi-day backcountry treks as well. A parking tag is required for trailheads.

guilin-yangshuo.overview: Walking in the Li River valley means navigating paved paths and dirt trails through flooded rice paddies and towering limestone karst peaks. Day hikes range from easy riverside strolls to steep, stair-heavy climbs up viewpoints like Moon Hill for panoramas of the jagged landscape. The terraced hillsides of Longji offer longer village-to-village routes. Fog and haze are most common from winter to early spring, and autumn is the clearest season.

months.1: January is cool, damp and often foggy, with haze dulling the views, and the stone steps up the karst peaks are slippery, but the valley paths remain open for walking.
months.2: February remains cool with drizzle and morning mist that blur the distant peaks, requiring care on steep limestone stairs, though the riverside trails are atmospheric.
months.3: March brings warmer temperatures, though morning mist still hangs over the limestone towers, and it is a good time to walk the trails around the rice terraces.
months.12: December cools down significantly, and fog and haze often dull the karst views, but the lower valley paths and terraced hillside routes remain fully walkable in brisk air.

havana.overview: Cuba has modest but rewarding trails through tropical forests, karst valleys, and mountain ranges. Day hikers explore the limestone mogotes of Viñales or the waterfalls of Topes de Collantes. The island's highest point, Pico Turquino, is a strenuous two-day trek that requires a local guide. The dry months from November to April provide the most reliable trail conditions.

hokkaido.overview: Hokkaido's volcanic peaks, caldera lakes and coastal trails are a magnet for those looking to escape the mainland's summer heat. Hikers head to Daisetsuzan National Park for alpine day hikes and multi-day traverses among steaming vents, or to the Shiretoko Peninsula, where brown bears forage and the Five Lakes ground trail needs a permit and bear briefing in bear season. Heavy winter snow keeps the season short.

hongkong.overview: Hong Kong offers surprisingly extensive walking trails that escape the dense city for green ridges and coastal views. The famous Dragon's Back is a day hike with sweeping ocean panoramas, while the 62-mile MacLehose Trail crosses the New Territories in ten sections. The best conditions are the cooler months from October through March.

iceland.overview: Iceland's trail network reaches volcanic craters, glacier tongues, and geothermal valleys that look like nowhere else on Earth. The country is famous for the Laugavegur trek, a 34-mile, multi-day journey through the rhyolite mountains of the central highlands, but day hikers find endless options, from the climb up Mount Esja near Reykjavík to the basalt columns of Svartifoss. The best long-distance trails are in the interior highlands and the remote Westfjords, and accessible only during a short summer window.
